claimBoundary: The released human-feedback evaluation path can reuse policies learned from an exact demo when evaluating another command attached to the same simulator sample. This is an evaluation-identifiability issue: it does not establish misconduct, and policy reuse is an intended system capability.

verifiedObservations.evidence: DbLv1Dataset creates one item for every sample-command pair and assigns IDs of the form scenario_s{sample}_c{command}. Different command IDs can therefore share the same complete simulator sample and random seed.
DbLv1DemoDataset selects a fixed list of exact IDs such as left_overtake_s0_c0 rather than reserving all commands that share the same sample or seed.
test_hf.py executes the demo set first, repeatedly refines each policy until success, and then evaluates non-demo dataset items. Only exact IDs already present in results are skipped.

Successful demo policies are added to a Chroma-backed repository. Test workers instantiate HumanFeedbackCGAgent with resume=true and retrieve semantically similar policies before generating the evaluated policy.

The project explicitly describes policy storage and retrieval for reuse as a core feature. The scientific question is therefore attribution of measured performance, not whether retrieval should exist.

The repository also exposes zero-shot/few-shot test_icl paths that do not use the human-feedback policy repository. Any finding must name the exact human-feedback protocol and must not be generalized to every LaMPilot result.

currentProtocolCanMix: policy retrieval for a semantically similar instruction
reuse of a policy learned on the same simulator initial state and seed
new code generation from the current context
missingSeparations: persistent repository versus repository reset before every test item
policy retrieved but hidden from generation versus stateless generation

credibleBuildPath: Construct canonical group keys from scenario config, sample index, and simulator seed before running any model.
Add retrieval traces that record policy IDs and similarity scores consumed by each test item without changing generated control code.
Run the same fixed model under exact-ID exclusion, repository-reset, sample-group holdout, seed-group holdout, and stateless ICL conditions.
Keep the command text and evaluation scenario fixed within paired comparisons, and bootstrap at the sample or seed group rather than at the command row.
Report policy-retrieval rate, success, collision, TTC, efficiency, and rank stability separately for instruction, sample, and seed generalization.

minimumFalsification.scope: At least three scenario families with demo IDs and multiple command paraphrases, including one lane-change or overtake task and one longitudinal-control task.
minimumFalsification.success: The released exact-ID protocol materially overstates performance relative to sample/seed group holdout, and the difference is mediated by retrieval of a policy learned from the same simulator state.
minimumFalsification.kill: Same-state non-demo commands do not retrieve or benefit from the demo policy, or strict sample/seed holdout leaves performance and method ranking unchanged.

strongBaselines: Released exact-ID exclusion with persistent repository
Repository reset before every evaluated command
Stateless zero-shot or few-shot code generation
remainingRisks: A performance drop under group holdout is not automatically leakage; it may quantify the intended value of policy reuse and should be reported as attribution rather than a defect.
The default README full-benchmark example uses test_icl rather than test_hf, so claims must remain protocol-specific.
Repository retrieval depends on external embeddings and LLM services; exact model revisions, temperature, prompts, and persisted repository bytes must be fixed.
The first items under a truncated, unshuffled test set may not include every demo scenario, so the complete benchmark or a preregistered scenario subset is required.
